Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for sending the updated order form. Legal has one procurement-level question before we can proceed: on the indemnification section for third-party IP claims, ACME needs clarity on the notice/evidence flow and who controls the defense. Specifically:

- If a third party asserts infringement, who at Redwood will be our point for receiving the notice and gathering evidence?
- Can Redwood commit to routing technical evidence requests to a named contact or team (we expect 24–48h turnaround from your side for basic logs/evidence)?
- Does Redwood propose to retain "defense control" (i.e., manage counsel and settlement decisions) or will ACME retain that control for claims that materially affect our business?

We understand Redwood's desire to retain some control for novel model-related claims; we just need the flow defined in the order form with SLAs and a named escalation path to procurement. Can you confirm and, if possible, provide a short excerpt we can attach to the order form?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our purchasing window closes next week.

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. Quick answers up front, then details below:

- Primary notice inbox: legal-notices@redwood.example.com (this routes to our legal ops + on-call counsel).
- Evidence point-of-contact: Security Evidence Team (security-evidence@redwood.example.com) — we can commit to an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and a target 48‑hour window for turnaround on basic logs/evidence.
- Defense control: Redwood proposes defense control for model and runtime-level claims but is open to an exception carve for claims that would reasonably require ACME to control settlement (e.g., material impact to ACME customers or data).

Proposed short excerpt you can attach to the order form: please find the suggested language below — we can also provide a redline doc if that helps.

--- proposed excerpt (for order form):
"Notice & evidence handling: Customer shall provide prompt written notice to Redwood at legal-notices@redwood.example.com upon becoming aware of any third-party claim alleging intellectual property infringement arising from the Customer's use of the Service. Redwood will acknowledge receipt within 24 hours. Redwood's Security Evidence Team will collaborate with Customer to identify, collect and provide relevant technical evidence; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver basic runtime/log evidence within 48 hours of receipt of the request.

Defense control & settlement: Redwood shall have the right to assume and control the defense of any third‑party claim alleging infringement of third-party intellectual property related to the Service, provided that Redwood shall not (i) settle any claim that requires Customer to admit liability or (ii) agree to any settlement that materially impairs Customer's rights or business without Customer's prior written consent. In the event a proposed settlement would have such an effect, Customer may assume control of the defense upon reasonable notice.
"

I'll loop in Kimberly and Laura for redlines and to confirm the SLA language. Happy to chat if you want to walk through the carve exceptions.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Legal (Commercial), Redwood Inference

Thanks for the draft language, Nikhil. I reviewed with Product and Security Ops and proposed a couple of restraint and escalation edits — attached is a redline (redline_defense-control_v2.docx). Key changes summarized:

1) Evidence SLA: tightened acknowledgement to 24h and added "priority classification" where evidence requests marked "priority" (security incident or regulatory) get 24h full response target; standard requests remain 48h.
2) Data scope: clarified we will provide technical/runtime evidence necessary to investigate the claim but will not produce raw customer data or PII unless legally compelled; added reference to redaction process and mutual redaction obligations.
3) Settlement carve: added a dual-notice path — Redwood can control defense, but if a proposed settlement would (a) require ACME to change customer-facing terms materially, (b) require ACME to pay monetary consideration exceeding $50k, or (c) materially impact ACME customers, ACME may request control and we will not unreasonably withhold.
4) Escalation path: included named escalation contacts (Legal Ops mgr: Kimberly Park; VP Legal: Nikhil Sharma) and a 48‑hour SLA for escalation response.

Sara — please see the redline and let us know if the $50k threshold is acceptable or if your procurement team needs alternative language (percentage of order value, etc.).
